newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pamodzi plans more buys after Aukland deal.
newsitem.headline: Pamodzi plans more buys after Aukland deal.

text.p: South Africa's Pamodzi Investment Holdings Ltd said it was planning eight new investments over the next two years, starting with the acquisition of a stake in health-care firm Aukland Investments.
"We plan to invest in eight companies within 18 months to two years...Aukland is our first investment," Pamodzi chairman Peter Vundla said at a presentation in Johannesburg.
The company earlier announced it had bought a 26 percent stake in Aukland for 46 million rand, by taking up shares renounced by the controlling shareholders in a 71 million rand rights issue.

Pamodzi, the Swahili word for "we are one", was established last year aiming to invest in companies in industries with good growth prospects, experienced management, strong prospects for cash generation and good returns.
"Aukland meets all these criteria," Vundla said.
Vundla said Pamodzi was in the market as a focused investment firm rather than a black empowerment group simply scouting for unbundling deals.

Founding shareholders include television talkshow host Felicia Mabuza-Suttle, Nike's South African franchise-holders Ndaba Ntsele and Solly Sithole, and Vundla, who was founder of Herdbouys, South Africa's first black-controlled advertising agency.

Aukland's assets consist of HospiPlan, managing 14 private hospitals, Othorsurge, a distributor of medical equipment, Unisurge, a surgical instrument distributor and Disamed, a pharmaceutical wholesaler.
Aukland chairman Hendri Wicht said the hospitals also had an alliance with private clinic group President Medical Investments Ltd, which increased their buying power.
The Aukland group plans to expand its hospital interests, outside South Africa, including Africa and further afield. It also planned to increase its product range.
Vundla said health services was a strong growth industry, with state hospitals unable to meet demand and the increasing numbers of South Africans covered by medical aid and insurance.
The market capitalisation of Aukland is about 120 million rand at current prices and will grow to about 200 million rand after the rights issue.
Aukland shares were last trading at 460 cents on Wednesday afternoon.
Vundla said Pamodzi was seriously studying three possible investments at present, but declined give details.
The company plans to focus on health care, sports and entertainment, information technology, logistics and facilities management.
